import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = []
    seen = set()
    corr_pairs = [(a, b) for a, b in [
        ("QOU16", "JVEP9"), ("ELVN3L", "QOU16"), ("ELVN3L", "MYQ13"),
        ("CSEL3", "JXF4"), ("UQR19", "KEE9A"), ("WJDN8", "QOU16"),
        ("CDKB7", "CSEL3"), ("ELVN3L", "JVEP9"), ("RXO7L", "ULZ3L"),
        ("FJFZ5", "BCM8"), ("JLI15", "QOU16"), ("RLTH9", "IJW10"),
        ("WJDN8", "ELVN3L"), ("QQCC2", "QOU16"), ("WUZ15A", "NAE17"),
        ("NIEG7", "CGCW12L"), ("CDKB7", "JXF4"), ("NVQE15B", "RXO7L"),
        ("JQXB1P", "WUZ15A"), ("WJDN8", "JVEP9")
    ] if a in feats.ids and b in feats.ids]
    
    for fid in feats.ids:
        is_dup = False
        for a, b in corr_pairs:
            if fid in [a, b] and a in seen or b in seen:
                is_dup = True
                break
        if not is_dup:
            seen.add(fid)
            keep.append(fid)
    
    # Calculate effect sizes and select top candidates
    effects = []
    for fid in keep:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col]
        effect = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        p_val = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)[1]
        effects.append((fid, abs(effect), abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size and statistical significance
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[3]))
    
    # Select drivers (features with large effect sizes)
    drivers = [f for f, _, _, _ in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Add main effects
    for fid in keep:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col]
        effect = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        
        # Include features with strong effects
        if abs(effect) > 0.1 or abs(t_stat) > 3:
            columns.append(fid)
            loadings[fid] = effect
    
    # Add interaction terms for highly correlated features
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in columns and b in columns:
            products.append((a, b))
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
